label: Access error node itself
summary: A function on a node error (an internal editor object of the game's interface) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the node error itself. The game documents no return type and no use for it. The game's own interface files use a function of this name only as PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, to pass a widget along as a data context.

label: Go to error
summary: A function on a node error that returns nothing and, going by its name, jumps to the node the error belongs to.
details: It is an internal tool of the game's interface editing; no game file uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Error message
summary: Text (a string) with the message of a node error.
details: Going by its name, it is the error text shown for a node in the game's internal node editor. No game file uses it.

label: Error node number
summary: A whole number (32-bit) that, going by its name, identifies the node the error is about.
details: The game documents nothing more, and no game file uses it.

label: Error itself
summary: A function on a node error that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the object itself. In game texts a function called Self follows other things, for example as CHARACTER.Self passed as an argument to GetName; that is only a hint, because those lines belong to other types.

label: Access line itself
summary: A function on a node line (a connecting line in an internal node editor of the game's interface) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the line itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Line color
summary: The color of a node line, as four numbers (a 4-part vector, most likely red, green, blue and opacity).
details: The meaning of the four parts is an assumption from the type name CVector4f and the function name. No game file uses it.

label: Line start point
summary: Going by its name, the start point of a node line, as two numbers (a 2-part vector).
details: Most likely a position (x and y). The game texts that contain the word From are ordinary sentences, not uses of this function. No game file uses it.

label: Owner node number
summary: A whole number (32-bit) that, going by its name, is the identifier of the node the line belongs to.
details: The game documents nothing more, and no game file uses it.

label: Line is highlighted
summary: Whether a node line is highlighted (a yes or no answer).
details: Going by its name, it tells whether the line is currently drawn as highlighted. The game texts that contain the word Highlighted are ordinary sentences about highlighted menu choices, not uses of this function.

label: Line itself
summary: A function on a node line that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the line itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Line end point
summary: Going by its name, the end point of a node line, as two numbers (a 2-part vector).
details: Most likely a position (x and y), the counterpart of From. The game texts that contain the word To are ordinary sentences, not uses of this function. No game file uses it.

label: Line width
summary: Going by its name, the width of a node line, as a decimal number.
details: Going by its name, it is the width the line is drawn with. No game file uses it.

label: Access pin itself
summary: A function on a node pin (a connection point on a node in an internal node editor) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the pin itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Pin color
summary: The color of a node pin, as four numbers (a 4-part vector, most likely red, green, blue and opacity).
details: The meaning of the four parts is an assumption from the type name CVector4f. No game file uses it. See also the type color, which is a separate function.

label: Pin drawn as connected
summary: Whether a node pin is drawn as connected (a yes or no answer).
details: Going by its name, it decides if the pin looks connected to another node. No game file uses it.

label: Pin is highlighted
summary: Whether a node pin is highlighted (a yes or no answer).
details: Going by its name, it tells if the pin is drawn highlighted. The game texts that contain the word Highlight are ordinary sentences, not uses of this function.

label: Inlined node connected
summary: Whether the inlined node of a pin is connected (a yes or no answer).
details: Going by its name, it checks if a node placed inline in the pin has a connection. The game documents nothing more, and no game file uses it.

label: Pin name
summary: The name of a node pin, as text.
details: Going by its name, it is the label of the pin. The game texts that contain the word Name are ordinary sentences, not uses of this function.

label: Pin itself
summary: A function on a node pin that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the pin itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Pin tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of a node pin.
details: Going by its name, it is the hover text shown for the pin. The game texts that contain the word Tooltip are ordinary sentences, not uses of this function.

label: Pin type color
summary: The color that stands for the data type of a node pin, as four numbers (a 4-part vector).
details: Going by its name, it is a color tied to the type of the pin. The meaning of the four parts (likely red, green, blue, opacity) is an assumption. No game file uses it.

label: Access node window itself
summary: A function on a node window (an internal node editor window of the game's interface) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the window itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Close node window
summary: A function that, going by its name, closes the node window; it returns nothing.
details: The game texts that contain the word Close are ordinary sentences (for example close relatives), not uses of this function. The game documents nothing more.

label: Open description dialog
summary: A function that, going by its name, opens a dialog for the description of the node window's content; it returns nothing.
details: The game documents nothing more, and no game file uses it.

label: Open name dialog
summary: A function that, going by its name, opens a dialog for the name of the node window's content; it returns nothing.
details: The game documents nothing more, and no game file uses it.

label: Node window itself
summary: A function on a node window that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the window itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Set description
summary: A function that, going by its name, sets the description of the node window's content; it returns nothing.
details: The game lists no arguments for it. The game documents nothing more, and no game file uses it.

label: Access dockable itself
summary: A function on a non-registered dockable (going by its name, a dockable panel not listed in a registry) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the panel itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Dockable ID
summary: The identifier of a non-registered dockable panel, as text.
details: Going by its name, it is the panel's ID. The game texts that call GetID, for example CHARACTER.GetID in debug tooltips, belong to the character type and are only a hint.

label: Dockable itself
summary: A function on a non-registered dockable that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the panel itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Access dummy context itself
summary: A function on the notification dummy context (a stand-in data object for notification interface elements) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Dummy context itself
summary: A function on the notification dummy context that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the object itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Access notification option
summary: A function on a notification option (one entry of the message settings) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the option itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Notification option name
summary: The display name of a notification option, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the message settings window, where it supplies the text shown for each option, written with a |U format switch. The game documents nothing more.

label: Notification option itself
summary: A function on a notification option that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the option itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Access nudger itself
summary: A function on the nudger (an internal map-object placement tool of the game) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the nudger itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: New map object type
summary: Creates a new, empty global map object type in the map editor's map objects tool; it returns nothing.
details: The map objects tool is what the game's code calls the nudger. Vanilla runs it from the 'Create new' button above the list of object types.

label: Delete selected objects
summary: Deletes the selected map objects in the map editor; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the button 'Delete selected map objects.', which is enabled only when a selected object is of a dynamic type.

label: Deselect objects
summary: Clears the selection of map objects in the map editor; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the button 'Deselect map objects if any are selected.', which is enabled only while an object is selected.

label: Focus camera on selection
summary: Moves the map editor's camera to the selected map objects or territories; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the focus button of the map objects tool.

label: Any object type expanded
summary: Whether any entry of the map objects tool's list is expanded.
details: Vanilla uses it for the 'Un/expand All' button: if any entry is expanded, a click collapses all, otherwise it expands all.

label: Any object type hidden
summary: Whether any entry of the map objects tool's list is hidden.
details: Vanilla uses it for the 'Un/hide All' button: if any entry is hidden, a click shows all, otherwise it hides all.

label: Any object type locked
summary: Whether any entry of the map objects tool's list is locked.
details: Vanilla uses it for the 'Un/lock All' button: if any entry is locked, a click unlocks all, otherwise it locks all.

label: Any object type selected
summary: Whether any map object type is selected in the map objects tool's list.
details: Vanilla enables the button 'Select all map objects of selected type(s).' only then.

label: Any object selected
summary: Whether any map object is selected on the map in the map editor.
details: Vanilla enables the buttons that deselect, randomly rotate, and toggle 'render underwater' and 'clamp to water level' for the selected objects only then.

label: Selection is dynamic type
summary: Whether any selected map object is of a dynamic type.
details: Vanilla enables the 'Delete selected map objects.' button only then. What makes an object type dynamic is not shown.

label: Multi spawn on
summary: Whether the map objects tool places several global object types at once.
details: Vanilla shows it as the state of the button 'Toggle ability of spawning multiple global object types at once.'; a click sets the opposite state.

label: On map object selected
summary: A function with one argument that, going by its name, is called when a map object gets selected; it returns nothing.
details: What the argument is (probably the selected object) is not documented. No game file uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The one argument; the game does not say what it is.

label: Select all objects
summary: Selects all map objects of the selected object types; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the select-all button of the map objects tool, which is enabled only while an object type is selected in the list.

label: Nudger itself
summary: A function on the nudger that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the nudger itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Expand all entries
summary: Expands or collapses all entries of the map objects tool's list; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the 'Un/expand All' button with the opposite of whether any entry is expanded.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Whether to expand (yes) or collapse (no) all entries.

label: Hide all entries
summary: Hides or shows all entries of the map objects tool's list; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the 'Un/hide All' button with the opposite of whether any entry is hidden.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Whether to hide (yes) or show (no) all entries.

label: Lock all entries
summary: Locks or unlocks all entries of the map objects tool's list; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the 'Un/lock All' button with the opposite of whether any entry is locked.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Whether to lock (yes) or unlock (no) all entries.

label: Set instances render pass
summary: A function that, going by its name, sets in which render pass the nudger's object instances are drawn; it returns nothing.
details: It takes no arguments according to the game. The game documents nothing more, and no game file uses it.

label: Hide map object
summary: A function with two arguments that, going by its name, hides or shows one map object; it returns nothing.
details: The arguments are not documented; most likely the object and a yes or no. No game file uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: First argument; going by the name, the map object.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Second argument; going by the name, whether it is hidden.
fields.values: not documented, probably yes or no

label: Lock map object
summary: A function with two arguments that, going by its name, locks or unlocks one map object; it returns nothing.
details: The arguments are not documented; most likely the object and a yes or no. No game file uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: First argument; going by the name, the map object.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Second argument; going by the name, whether it is locked.
fields.values: not documented, probably yes or no

label: Lock only this map object
summary: A function with two arguments that, going by its name, locks one map object exclusively; it returns nothing.
details: What exclusive means (likely that other objects are not locked at the same time) and the arguments are not documented. No game file uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: First argument; going by the name, the map object.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Second argument; going by the name, whether it is locked.
fields.values: not documented, probably yes or no

label: Set multi spawn
summary: Switches placing several global object types at once on or off; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the multi spawn button with the opposite of the current state, so a click toggles it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: yes or no (vanilla passes the opposite of the current state)

label: Toggle clamp to water
summary: Switches the 'clamp to water level' setting of the selected map objects; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the matching toolbar button, which is enabled only while an object is selected. Going by the setting's name, it keeps the objects at the water's surface.

label: Toggle render underwater
summary: Switches the 'render underwater' setting of the selected map objects; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the matching toolbar button, which is enabled only while an object is selected. Going by the setting's name, it decides whether the objects are drawn below the water.

label: Access map object entry
summary: A function on a map object entry of a nudger layer that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the entry itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Map object name
summary: The name of a map object entry in the map editor's territory list, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of the entry's button in the map objects tool's territory view.

label: Auto placement failed
summary: Whether automatic placement failed for this map object entry.
details: Vanilla shows an error icon on the entry while it is true, with the tooltip that the object could not be auto-spawned, probably for lack of free surface.

label: Is object locked
summary: Whether this map object entry is locked against moving.
details: Vanilla shows it as the padlock box of the entry, whose tooltip is 'Lock ability of moving this object.'; a click sets the opposite state.

label: Is object selected
summary: Whether this map object entry is selected.
details: Vanilla shows it as the pressed state of the entry's button in the territory view.

label: Select object entry
summary: Selects this map object entry; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it when the entry's button in the territory view is clicked.

label: Map object entry itself
summary: A function on a map object entry that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the entry itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Lock object
summary: Locks this map object entry against moving, or unlocks it; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the entry's padlock box with the opposite of the current state, so a click toggles the lock.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: yes or no (vanilla passes the opposite of the current state)

label: Access nudger map content
summary: A function on the nudger's map content interface that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the object itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Auto place objects
summary: Places all map objects automatically in the selected territories; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the toolbar button whose tooltip says only territories not marked as complete are affected. The button is enabled only when auto nudging (automatic placement) is supported and ready and at least one territory is selected.

label: Auto placement progress
summary: How far the preparation for automatic placement of map objects has come, as a decimal number.
details: Vanilla shows it followed by a % sign in the tooltip of the spinner that says auto nudging is not available yet and asks to wait.

label: Placement preview on
summary: Whether the preview of the random placement mask is shown for the selected map objects.
details: Vanilla shows it as the state of the button 'Visualize the random placement mask for currently selected map objects.'; a click sets the opposite state.

label: Auto placement ready
summary: Whether automatic placement of map objects is ready to run.
details: Vanilla enables the auto placement button only then (together with other conditions). While it is not ready, a spinner with the progress percentage shows in its place.

label: Placement settings open
summary: Whether the panel of game-specific settings for automatic placement is open.
details: Vanilla shows it as the state of the settings button and shows the 'Game specific properties' panel only while it is true.

label: Auto placement supported
summary: Whether automatic placement of map objects is supported.
details: Vanilla enables the auto placement button and shows the waiting spinner only when it is true. What decides support is not shown.

label: Nudger map content itself
summary: A function on the nudger's map content interface that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the object itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Set placement preview
summary: Shows or hides the preview of the random placement mask; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the preview button with the opposite of the current state, so a click toggles it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: yes or no (vanilla passes the opposite of the current state)

label: Open placement settings
summary: Opens or closes the panel of game-specific settings for automatic placement; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the settings button with the opposite of the current state, so a click toggles the panel.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: yes or no (vanilla passes the opposite of the current state)

label: Access property list panel
summary: A function on the nudger's map object property list panel that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the panel itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Delete object type
summary: Removes the selected map object type in the map editor's property panel; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla runs it from the 'Delete Object Type' button, whose tooltip says the removal is committed only when saved.

label: Has object type
summary: Whether a map object type is selected in the map editor's property panel.
details: When it is false, vanilla shows 'No map object type selected'. When it is true and the type is not made by a generator script, it shows the type's properties.

label: Is generated type
summary: Whether the map object type selected in the map editor's object panel is made by a generator script (yes or no).
details: The engine's map editor shows a note when it is true: such a type is defined through a generator script and is painted with the Map Object Painter tool. The panel's property list is shown only when a type is selected and this is false. It is a tool of the map editor, not of the game itself.

label: Property list panel itself
summary: A function on the property list panel that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the panel itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Access nudger mode
summary: A function on a nudger mode (one of the working modes of the nudger tool) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the mode itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Object tool is active
summary: Whether the map editor's map objects tool (the nudger) is the tool currently chosen (yes or no).
details: The engine's map editor uses it to show the Map Objects Editor button in its toolbox as pressed. It is a tool of the map editor, not of the game itself.

label: Nudger mode itself
summary: A function on a nudger mode that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the mode itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Access object browser
summary: A function on the object browser (a debug tool of the game's interface for listing objects) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the browser itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Copy as CSV
summary: A function that, going by its name, copies the browser's listed objects as comma-separated text; it returns nothing.
details: The game documents nothing more, and no game file uses it.

label: Create new preset
summary: A function that, going by its name, creates a new preset (a saved set of browser settings); it returns nothing.
details: The game documents nothing more, and no game file uses it.

label: Delete selected preset
summary: A function that, going by its name, deletes the selected preset of the object browser; it returns nothing.
details: Vanilla has a function of the same name on another type (a character selection list) used for a button click, which is only a hint here.

label: Force update
summary: A function that, going by its name, makes the browser refresh its list at once; it returns nothing.
details: Compare RequestUpdate. No game file uses it.

label: Filter text
summary: The text currently used as the browser's filter.
details: It is set with SetFilterString. No game file uses it.

label: Number of filtered objects
summary: A whole number that, going by its name, counts the objects that pass the filter.
details: Compare GetNumObjectsTotal. No game file uses it.

label: Total number of objects
summary: A whole number that, going by its name, counts all objects of the browser, before filtering.
details: Compare GetNumObjectsFiltered. No game file uses it.

label: Presets
summary: The presets of the object browser; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it gives the list of saved presets, probably of the ObjectPreset type. No game file uses it.

label: Providers
summary: The providers of the object browser (the sources of the objects it lists); the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it gives a list, probably of ObjectProvider entries. No game file uses it.

label: Selected provider
summary: The selected provider of the browser, given as two whole numbers (a 2-part integer vector).
details: What the two numbers mean (perhaps an index and a count) is not documented. No game file uses it.

label: Selected view
summary: The selected view of the browser, given as two whole numbers (a 2-part integer vector).
details: What the two numbers mean is not documented. No game file uses it.

label: Views
summary: The views of the object browser; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it gives a list, probably of ObjectBrowserView entries. No game file uses it.

label: Has config
summary: Whether the object browser has a configuration (a yes or no answer).
details: What the configuration is is not documented. No game file uses it.

label: Is object selected
summary: Whether the given object is selected in the browser (a yes or no answer).
details: It takes one argument, most likely the object or its index; the game does not say. No game file uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The one argument; going by the name, the object to check.

label: Output is flattened
summary: Whether the browser's output is flattened (a yes or no answer).
details: What flattened means here is not documented. It can be switched with ToggleOutputFlattened. No game file uses it.

label: Waiting for provider
summary: Whether the browser is still waiting for its provider to deliver objects (a yes or no answer).
details: Going by its name. No game file uses it.

label: Rename selected preset
summary: A function that, going by its name, renames the selected preset; it returns nothing.
details: The game lists no arguments for it. No game file uses it.

label: Refresh object list
summary: Makes the engine's object browser refresh the list it shows; it returns nothing.
details: The object browser (a debug tool of the engine) calls it when the query text is confirmed with Return and from a button whose tooltip says it forces an update of the list with the query set above. It runs after the query text and filter are applied.

label: Save current changes
summary: A function that, going by its name, saves the changes made to the current preset; it returns nothing.
details: The game documents nothing more, and no game file uses it.

label: Save defaults
summary: A function that, going by its name, saves the current settings as the browser's defaults; it returns nothing.
details: The game documents nothing more, and no game file uses it.

label: Select provider
summary: A function that, going by its name, selects a provider for the browser; it returns nothing.
details: The game lists no arguments for it. No game file uses it.

label: Select view
summary: A function that, going by its name, selects a view for the browser; it returns nothing.
details: The game lists no arguments for it. No game file uses it.

label: Object browser itself
summary: A function on the object browser that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the browser itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Set filter text
summary: A function that, going by its name, sets the browser's filter text; it returns nothing.
details: The game lists no arguments for it. The text is read with GetFilterString. No game file uses it.

label: Set object selected
summary: A function with one argument that, going by its name, selects an object in the browser; it returns nothing.
details: What the argument is (likely the object) is not documented. No game file uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The one argument; going by the name, the object to select.

label: Set selected preset
summary: A function with one argument that, going by its name, makes a preset the selected one; it returns nothing.
details: What the argument is (likely the preset) is not documented. No game file uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The one argument; going by the name, the preset to select.

label: Toggle object selected
summary: A function with one argument that, going by its name, flips the selection of an object; it returns nothing.
details: What the argument is (likely the object) is not documented. No game file uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The one argument; going by the name, the object whose selection flips.

label: Toggle flattened output
summary: A function that, going by its name, switches the flattened output on or off; it returns nothing.
details: The state is read with IsOutputFlattened. No game file uses it.

label: Access browser view
summary: A function on an object browser view that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the view itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: View name
summary: The name of an object browser view, as text.
details: Going by its name. The game texts that contain the word Name are ordinary sentences, not uses of this function.

label: Browser view itself
summary: A function on an object browser view that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the view itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Access plugin entries
summary: The plugin entries of the object inspector (a debug tool that shows the details of an object); the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the list of plugins, probably ObjectInspectorPlugin entries. No game file uses it.

label: Access object inspector
summary: A function on the object inspector that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the inspector itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Inspected object name
summary: The name of the object being inspected, as text.
details: Going by its name. A vanilla debug window (the watch window) calls a function of this name, written WatchWindow.GetObjectName, which is only a hint.

label: Inspected object type
summary: The type name of the object being inspected, as text.
details: Going by its name. Game texts that call GetTypeName belong to other types and are only a hint.

label: Object inspector itself
summary: A function on the object inspector that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the inspector itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Access inspector panel
summary: A function on the object inspector's dockable panel that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the panel itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Detach
summary: A function that, going by its name, detaches the inspector panel from its dock; it returns nothing.
details: The state is read with IsAttached. No game file uses it.

label: Is attached
summary: Whether the inspector panel is attached to its dock (a yes or no answer).
details: Going by its name. Detach is the matching action. No game file uses it.

label: Inspector panel itself
summary: A function on the inspector's dockable panel that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the panel itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Access inspector plugin
summary: A function on an object inspector plugin that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the plugin itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Plugin error message
summary: The error message of an object inspector plugin, as text.
details: Going by its name; HasError tells whether there is one. A vanilla login window calls a function of this name on another type (LoginView), which is only a hint.

label: Plugin title
summary: The title of an object inspector plugin, as text.
details: Going by its name. Game texts that call GetTitle belong to other types (for example titles of rulers) and are only a hint.

label: Plugin has error
summary: Whether the plugin has an error (a yes or no answer).
details: The message is read with GetErrorMessage. No game file uses it.

label: Inspector plugin itself
summary: A function on an inspector plugin that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the plugin itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Access preset
summary: A function on an object browser preset that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the preset itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Preset is selected
summary: Whether this preset is the selected one (a yes or no answer).
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses IsSelected on other types (save game items, bookmark items, units) to show an item as pressed, which is only a hint here.

label: Preset name
summary: The name of the preset, as text.
details: Going by its name. No game file uses it.

label: Preset itself
summary: A function on a preset that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the preset itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Access object provider
summary: A function on an object provider (a source of objects for the object browser) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the provider itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Provider name
summary: The name of an object provider, as text.
details: Going by its name. The game texts that contain the word Name are ordinary sentences, not uses of this function.

label: Request provider update
summary: A function that, going by its name, asks the provider to refresh its objects; it returns nothing.
details: No game file uses it.

label: Provider itself
summary: A function on an object provider that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the provider itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Access obligation container
summary: A function on an obligation container (a group of obligations in the vassal contract window) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the container itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Obligation group icon
summary: The icon of an obligation container, going by its name; it returns text.
details: Vanilla puts it right after the container's name in the window for changing a vassal's contract, for example [ObligationContainerData.GetName] [ObligationContainerData.GetIcon]. The game documents nothing more.

label: Obligation group name
summary: The name of an obligation container, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a heading in the window for changing a vassal's contract, alone or followed by the container's icon.

label: Obligation container itself
summary: A function on an obligation container that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Going by its name, it is the container itself. Game texts show a function called Self after other things, for example CHARACTER.Self passed to a name function; that is only a hint, as those lines belong to other types.

label: Should show
summary: Whether the obligation container should be shown for a given contract (a yes or no answer).
details: Vanilla uses it to set whether a container is visible in the vassal contract window, passing the contract preview of that window as the argument. What decides the answer is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The contract to check; vanilla passes the contract preview of the window.

label: Access obligation level
summary: A function on an obligation level (one setting of a vassal contract obligation) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the level itself. The game documents no return type. The sample interface lines the game gives for this name show it only on another type (PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, passed as a data context), which is a hint, not a use of this function.

label: Obligation level description
summary: The description of an obligation level, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a tooltip in the vassal detail window and as the text of a shared tooltip. The game documents nothing more.

label: Obligation level effects
summary: Going by its name, the text that lists the effects of an obligation level.
details: Vanilla uses it as a text in the shared tooltip (cooltip). The game documents nothing more.

label: Obligation level name
summary: The name of an obligation level, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it on the map icon layer, in the vassal detail window and in the government administration window.
